faq.a: Advance tax is the income tax paid in advance during the financial year itself, rather than as a lump sum at the year-end. It applies if your estimated tax liability, after TDS, is ₹10,000 or more.

faq.q: How often does the RBI Monetary Policy Committee meet?
faq.a: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is mandated to meet at least four times a year, but typically meets six times a year, i.e., bi-monthly.

faq.q: What is the role of SEBI?
faq.a: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) is the regulatory body for the securities market in India. Its primary role is to protect the interests of investors in securities and to promote the development of, and to regulate, the securities market.

faq.q: Will new SEBI regulations affect my existing mutual fund investments?
faq.a: Yes, new SEBI regulations can affect existing mutual fund investments, especially concerning aspects like expense ratios, disclosure norms, or scheme categorisation, which can indirectly impact your returns or risk profile.

faq.q: What are the consequences of missing GST filing deadlines?
faq.a: Missing GST filing deadlines can lead to late fees and interest on the unpaid tax amount. Persistent non-compliance can also result in penalties and legal action from tax authorities.

faq.q: Where can I find official information on income tax deadlines?
faq.a: Official information on income tax deadlines and regulations can be found on the Income Tax Department's official website, incometax.gov.in.

faq.q: How does a repo rate change impact home loan EMIs?
faq.a: When the RBI increases the repo rate, banks typically increase their lending rates, which can lead to higher EMIs for home loans linked to external benchmarks or MCLR. Conversely, a rate cut can reduce EMIs.
